message.content: {"caption":"A bordered text panel presents instructions for answering benchmark questions using retrieved evidence.","description":"A rectangular panel with a thin blue border contains a bold teal heading, “Prompt 3: Answering with fixed evidence.” Black text below says to answer a benchmark question using the memory workspace and retrieved evidence, treating memory as a hint or index and retrieved evidence as authoritative. It directs the model to prefer retrieved evidence when it conflicts with memory; compare older and newer retrieved values for exact-fact questions; and, for current/latest/how-many/average questions, use the latest confirmed matching mention by turn order rather than an older or planned value. If asked for first or original values, give the original and mention later updates only if useful. If evidence does not support an answer, say the available memory or evidence is insufficient. It asks for concise answers that include relevant exact dates, versions, names, and constraints. The listed inputs are a JSON memory view, the last five Q/A pairs from the evaluation session, retrieved chunks, and a question. No arrows, symbols, or chart elements are present.","figure_type":"other","chart_values":[]}
